docs.title: vergil-fixture-python-app
docs.text: This is a Vergil test fixture. It has no users. It is a small, real Python command-line application that Vergil itself is tested against.

docs.title: What it is for
docs.text:
The fixture is managed exactly like a real Vergil Python application, with every fleet automation enabled. Each fixture run drives it through Vergil's full cycle for real: a change, a pull request, CI, a merge, a release, and a validation of the result. A run that goes red shows a Vergil regression before a real repository meets it.

It exercises:

  • the Python vrg-validate gates: ruff, mypy, ty, pytest at 100% branch coverage, pip-audit and the license check;
  • the CI workflows, the docs site build and its publishing to GitHub Pages;
  • the dependency audit and updates, through three real runtime dependencies: rich, PyYAML and packaging;
  • the tagged release of an application.

Nothing it does reaches a package registry.

The design is in the epic's spec, Language fixture repos.

docs.title: The program
docs.text:
Usage describes each of the subcommands of vergil-fixture-python-app.

The program grows by one small change per fixture run, so it is built to take one more subcommand without restructuring: a subcommand is one module under src/vergil_fixture_python_app/commands/, one entry in its COMMANDS tuple, and its tests.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
The fixture is never published to a package registry. Run it from a clone:

git clone https://github.com/vergil-project/vergil-fixture-python-app.git
cd vergil-fixture-python-app
uv sync
uv run vergil-fixture-python-app greet Ada

Or install it as a tool straight from the repository:

uv tool install git+https://github.com/vergil-project/vergil-fixture-python-app
vergil-fixture-python-app --help

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
As in every Vergil repository, validation is one command, run in the project's dev container:

vrg-container-run -- vrg-validate

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
vergil-fixture-python-app <command> [arguments]

vergil-fixture-python-app --help lists the commands, and vergil-fixture-python-app <command> --help describes one.

docs.title: Exit status
docs.text: Status Meaning 0 The command succeeded. 1 The command failed. The reason is on stderr, after vergil-fixture-python-app:. 2 The command line was not valid.

docs.title: greet NAME
docs.text:
Print a greeting. The name is printed exactly as given.

$ vergil-fixture-python-app greet Ada
Hello, Ada

An empty or whitespace-only name fails.

docs.title: compare LEFT RIGHT
docs.text:
Order two versions by the PEP 440 rules, using packaging. It prints the two versions as given, with <, > or == between them.

$ vergil-fixture-python-app compare 1.2.0 1.10.0
1.2.0 < 1.10.0
$ vergil-fixture-python-app compare 1.0 1.0.0
1.0 == 1.0.0

A version that is not valid under PEP 440 fails.

docs.title: keys FILE
docs.text:
Read a YAML file with PyYAML and list its top-level keys, in file order, with the type of each value, as a rich table under the file's path.

$ vergil-fixture-python-app keys config.yaml
config.yaml
┏━━━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━┓
┃ Key     ┃ Type ┃
┡━━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━┩
│ name    │ str  │
│ version │ int  │
└─────────┴──────┘

A file that cannot be read, is not valid YAML, or does not hold a mapping fails.

docs.title: sort [--reverse] VERSION...
docs.text:
List one or more versions in PEP 440 order, oldest first, one per line, each printed as given. --reverse (-r) lists the newest first. Equal versions, such as 1.0 and 1.0.0, keep the order they were given in.

$ vergil-fixture-python-app sort 1.10.0 1.2.0 1.0.0rc1
1.0.0rc1
1.2.0
1.10.0
$ vergil-fixture-python-app sort --reverse 1.10.0 1.2.0
1.10.0
1.2.0

A version that is not valid under PEP 440 fails, and nothing is printed.

docs.title: normalize VERSION...
docs.text:
Print the PEP 440 normal form of one or more versions, using packaging, one per line in the order given. The normal form drops a leading v and a zero epoch, lowercases, and spells pre-, post- and development releases and local labels the standard way.

$ vergil-fixture-python-app normalize V1.0 1.0-alpha.1 1.0-1 1.0+Ubuntu-1
1.0
1.0a1
1.0.post1
1.0+ubuntu.1

A version that is not valid under PEP 440 fails, and nothing is printed.

docs.title: latest [--stable] VERSION...
docs.text:
Print the newest of one or more versions by the PEP 440 rules, using packaging, printed as given. Of equal versions, such as 1.0 and 1.0.0, the first given is printed. --stable (-s) skips pre-releases and development releases.

$ vergil-fixture-python-app latest 1.2.0 1.10.0 2.0rc1
2.0rc1
$ vergil-fixture-python-app latest --stable 1.2.0 1.10.0 2.0rc1
1.10.0

A version that is not valid under PEP 440 fails, and so does --stable when every version given is a pre-release or development release.

docs.title: match SPECIFIER VERSION...
docs.text:
Print the versions that a PEP 440 version specifier, such as >=1.2,<2 or ~=1.4, allows, using packaging, one per line in the order given, each printed as given. A pre-release or development release is judged by the specifier like any other version.

$ vergil-fixture-python-app match '>=1.2,<2' 1.0 1.10.0 2.0 1.2
1.10.0
1.2

A specifier or version that is not valid under PEP 440 fails, and nothing is printed. So does a run in which no version matches.

docs.title: bump PART VERSION
docs.text:
Print the next major, minor or micro release after a PEP 440 version, using packaging. The named release number goes up by one and the ones after it become 0. The result always has three release numbers: a shorter version is padded with 0 and a longer one is cut to three. Any pre-release, post-release, development or local part is dropped, and an epoch is kept.

$ vergil-fixture-python-app bump minor 1.2.3
1.3.0
$ vergil-fixture-python-app bump micro 1.2
1.2.1

A version that is not valid under PEP 440 fails, and so does a part other than major, minor or micro.

docs.title: base VERSION...
docs.text:
Print the base version of each of one or more PEP 440 versions, using packaging, one per line in the order given. The base version is the epoch and the release numbers only, in normal form: any pre-release, post-release, development or local part is dropped. Unlike bump, the release numbers are neither padded nor cut.

$ vergil-fixture-python-app base 1.2.3rc1 2.0.post1 '1!3.1.dev4'
1.2.3
2.0
1!3.1

A version that is not valid under PEP 440 fails, and nothing is printed.

docs.title: public VERSION...
docs.text:
Print the public version of each of one or more PEP 440 versions, using packaging, one per line in the order given. The public version is the version in normal form without its local label (the part after +). Unlike base, it keeps every other part: the epoch and any pre-release, post-release or development part.

$ vergil-fixture-python-app public 1.2.3+local.7 2.0rc1+abc 3.1
1.2.3
2.0rc1
3.1

A version that is not valid under PEP 440 fails, and nothing is printed.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• add the CLI with greet, compare and keys subcommands, its tests and docs (#2) A small argparse CLI with one module per subcommand, runtime dependencies rich, PyYAML and packaging, tests at 100% branch coverage, the docs site pages and the README. Ref vergil-project/vergil-fixture-python-app#1.

  • add the sort subcommand and roll rich back in uv.lock (#6)

  • feat(cli): add the sort subcommand, listing versions in PEP 440 order

  • build(deps): roll rich back to 14.1.0 in uv.lock for the fixture run's dependency update

The declared range in pyproject.toml stays rich>=13.0, so the release's dependency update has a guaranteed upgrade to make.

CI Evidence: All gates passed — full audit bundle available. Download →

docs.title: CI
docs.text: • move the nightly ops cron to the 01:xx UTC hour (#12) GitHub's schedule events fire 7 to 9 hours late, landing the 06:xx UTC nightly run in the US Eastern working morning. Moving it to 01:06 UTC keeps it overnight despite the lag. The minute (the per-repo stagger) is unchanged.
